accepted.s: For how many consecutive years did India record a current account surplus during the period 2001-02 to 2003-04?
accepted.x: India recorded a current account surplus for three consecutive years from 2001-02 to 2003-04.
accepted.tq: Match the duration directly with the specified financial-year range.
accepted.sec: Current account deficit - trend, surplus years, reasons  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s current account position:
1. The current account recorded a surplus in the fourth quarter of 2023-24.
2. The surplus was driven by a surge in services exports.
3. The surplus was primarily caused by a sharp rise in gold imports.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the surplus was associated with a surge in services exports, not a rise in gold imports.
accepted.tq: Separate the stated cause of a surplus from a plausible but opposite trade-pressure factor.
accepted.sec: Current account deficit - trend, surplus years, reasons  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the first quarter of 2026-27, India’s current account deficit was reported at approximately:
o: $4.2 billion, or 0.5 per cent of GDP
$13.2 billion, or 1.3 per cent of GDP
$1.3 billion, or 0.2 per cent of GDP
$25.2 billion, or 0.6 per cent of GDP
accepted.x: In Q1 2026-27, the CAD was $4.2 billion, equivalent to 0.5 per cent of GDP, compared with 0.4 per cent a year earlier.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the quarterly figure from the full-year and other quarterly CAD figures.
accepted.sec: Current account deficit - trend, surplus years, reasons  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the major components of India’s current account position in the first quarter of 2026-27?
o: Merchandise gap of $86.1 billion, net services of $51.6 billion and net primary income outgo of $10.5 billion
Merchandise gap of $51.6 billion, net services of $86.1 billion and net primary income outgo of $10.5 billion
Merchandise gap of $25.2 billion, net services of $51.6 billion and net primary income outgo of $13.2 billion
Merchandise gap of $86.1 billion, net services of $10.5 billion and net primary income outgo of $51.6 billion
accepted.x: The Q1 FY27 figures were a merchandise gap of $86.1 billion, net services of $51.6 billion and net primary income outgo of $10.5 billion.
accepted.tq: Use component-value matching to prevent interchange of closely related external-sector figures.
accepted.sec: Current account deficit - trend, surplus years, reasons  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The record services surplus of $188.8 billion in FY25 financed approximately what proportion of the merchandise deficit?
accepted.x: The record services surplus of $188.8 billion in FY25 financed about two-thirds of the merchandise deficit. Remittances also acted as a cushion.
accepted.tq: Identify the comparative proportion rather than treating the services surplus as full financing of the merchandise deficit.
accepted.sec: Current account deficit - trend, surplus years, reasons  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The external-sector recovery in FY24 was mainly associated with:
o: A decline in remittances and a rise in primary-income outgo
A complete elimination of the merchandise deficit
Moderation in merchandise exports along with a sharp fall in imports
A sharp rise in merchandise imports and a fall in services exports
accepted.x: The FY24 external-sector recovery came from moderation in merchandise exports accompanied by a sharp fall in imports.
accepted.tq: Select the precise cause-effect combination and reject reversed trade trends.
accepted.sec: Current account deficit - trend, surplus years, reasons  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following are structural causes of India’s current account deficit?
1. Dependence on imported oil and gold
2. Low export competitiveness
3. Savings-investment gap
4. Temporary global slowdown alone
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Imported oil and gold, low export competitiveness and the savings-investment gap are structural causes. A temporary global slowdown is a cyclical cause, not a structural cause.
accepted.tq: Classify permanent structural pressures separately from temporary cyclical shocks.
accepted.sec: Current account deficit - trend, surplus years, reasons  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly describes the RBI’s monthly external-sector data mentioned for June and July 2026?
o: June CAD of $20.8 billion; July capital-account surplus of $6.2 billion and overall BoP surplus of $27.7 billion
June CAD of $27.7 billion; July capital-account surplus of $6.2 billion and overall BoP surplus of $20.8 billion
June CAD of $6.2 billion; July capital-account surplus of $27.7 billion and overall BoP surplus of $20.8 billion
June CAD of $6.2 billion; July capital-account deficit of $27.7 billion and overall BoP deficit of $20.8 billion
accepted.x: The RBI reported a CAD of $6.2 billion in June 2026. In July 2026, the capital account showed a $27.7 billion surplus and the overall BoP showed a $20.8 billion surplus.
accepted.tq: Keep the month and the three external-account values paired correctly.
accepted.sec: Current account deficit - trend, surplus years, reasons  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) were created by the International Monetary Fund in:
accepted.x: The IMF created SDRs in 1969 to supplement the official reserves of its member countries.
accepted.tq: Recall the institutional origin and year of creation without confusing it with later currency or convertibility milestones.
accepted.sec: SDR - nature, form, basket  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to Special Drawing Rights, consider the following statements:
1. SDR is an interest-bearing reserve asset.
2. SDRs are exchangeable for freely usable currencies.
3. SDRs are physical gold coins issued by the IMF.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: SDRs are interest-bearing reserve assets exchangeable for freely usable currencies. They are not physical gold coins; they are often described as ‘paper gold’.
accepted.tq: Reject the literal interpretation of a popular descriptive term such as ‘paper gold’.
accepted.sec: SDR - nature, form, basket  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The form in which Special Drawing Rights are maintained is best described as:
accepted.x: SDRs exist as book-keeping or accounting entries in the IMF’s records; they are not physical currency or metal.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the reserve-asset concept from a physical medium of payment.
accepted.sec: SDR - nature, form, basket  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included in the SDR basket?
accepted.x: The SDR basket contains the US dollar, euro, Chinese renminbi, Japanese yen and pound sterling. The Indian rupee is not included.
accepted.tq: Find the outsider in a named five-currency basket.
accepted.sec: SDR - nature, form, basket  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Chinese renminbi was added to the SDR basket in:
accepted.x: The Chinese renminbi was added to the IMF’s SDR basket in 2016.
accepted.tq: Use the exact inclusion year rather than the years associated with other IMF reforms.
accepted.sec: SDR - nature, form, basket  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes FERA from FEMA?
o: FERA was a restrictive criminal law, whereas FEMA is a liberal civil law concerned with management and regulation
FERA followed a liberal approach, whereas FEMA imposed strict control over outflow
FERA was a civil law, whereas FEMA was a criminal law
Both FERA and FEMA were identical in nature and approach
accepted.x: FERA 1973 was restrictive and criminal in nature, focusing on control of foreign exchange outflow. FEMA 1999 is a civil law based on management and regulation with a more liberal approach.
accepted.tq: Compare the legal character and policy approach of the two paired statutes.
accepted.sec: FERA to FEMA  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding FEMA:
1. Its replacement was proposed in the 1997-98 Budget.
2. FEMA was enacted in 1999.
3. FEMA came into force on 1 June 2000.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: replacement was proposed in the 1997-98 Budget, FEMA was enacted in 1999, and it came into force on 1 June 2000.
accepted.tq: Track a law through proposal, enactment and commencement instead of treating them as one date.
accepted.sec: FERA to FEMA  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the external capital-flow position of India in FY26?
o: FPI outflows of $44.0 billion and net FDI of $16.4 billion
FPI outflows of $16.4 billion and net FDI of $6.9 billion
FPI inflows of $6.9 billion and net FDI of $16.4 billion
FPI inflows of $16.4 billion and net FDI of $44.0 billion
accepted.x: In FY26, FPIs withdrew $16.4 billion, while net FDI was only $6.9 billion. A separate estimate placed FY26 net FDI at $7.6 billion.
accepted.tq: Check both the direction of the flow and the value before selecting the option.
accepted.sec: Capital flight and external vulnerability  [other exams]

accepted.s: During 2022-23 to 2025-26, gross equity FDI of $317.8 billion was reduced by which combination of outflows?
o: Repatriation and disinvestment of $44.0 billion and dividends of $127 billion
Repatriation and disinvestment of $178.9 billion and dividends of $118.9 billion
Repatriation and disinvestment of $317.8 billion and dividends of $6.9 billion
Repatriation and disinvestment of $118.9 billion and dividends of $178.9 billion
accepted.x: Gross equity FDI was $317.8 billion, while repatriation and disinvestment amounted to $178.9 billion and dividends to $118.9 billion.
accepted.tq: Match each outflow category with its exact figure rather than merely adding the two amounts.
accepted.sec: Capital flight and external vulnerability  [other exams]

accepted.s: The post-1991 pattern in which capital surplus covered the current account deficit was disrupted because:
o: The IMF abolished SDR allocations after 2024
Services exports became permanently negative after 2024
Capital inflows shrank from the middle of 2024
accepted.x: Since mid-2024, capital inflows have shrunk, breaking the earlier pattern of capital surplus financing the current account deficit.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated turning point and avoid substituting unrelated external-sector developments.
accepted.sec: Capital flight and external vulnerability  [other exams]

accepted.s: The special FCNR(B) deposit scheme in July 2026 was described as a ‘one-time comfort’ because it:
o: Converted all foreign portfolio investment into foreign direct investment
Eliminated India’s merchandise deficit permanently through higher exports
Reduced India’s external debt to zero
Drew $127 billion in NRI deposits and temporarily supported the capital account and overall BoP surplus
accepted.x: The scheme drew $127 billion in NRI deposits, contributing to a $27.7 billion capital-account surplus and a $20.8 billion overall BoP surplus. Its support was viewed as temporary or one-time.
accepted.tq: Link a policy instrument to its immediate balance-of-payments effect without inferring a permanent structural change.
accepted.sec: Capital flight and external vulnerability  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following are safeguards against external vulnerability?
1. Maintaining adequate foreign-exchange reserves sufficient for import cover
2. Keeping short-term external debt low
3. Reducing reliance on volatile FPI and debt flows
4. Increasing dependence on hot money
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Adequate reserves, low short-term debt and reduced dependence on volatile FPI and debt flows strengthen external resilience. Greater dependence on hot money increases vulnerability.
accepted.tq: Identify the protective measures and reject the deliberately reversed safeguard.
accepted.sec: Capital flight and external vulnerability  [other exams]

accepted.s: How do increases in US Federal Reserve interest rates and a strong US dollar generally affect emerging markets such as India?
o: They automatically increase India’s net FDI
They raise US yields, attract hot money away from emerging markets and weaken the rupee
They reduce US yields and cause capital to flow into emerging markets
They eliminate exchange-rate volatility in emerging markets
accepted.x: US rate hikes and a strong dollar raise US yields, encouraging hot-money outflows from emerging markets and putting downward pressure on the rupee.
accepted.tq: Follow the capital-flow chain from interest-rate differential to exchange-rate pressure.
accepted.sec: Capital flight and external vulnerability  [other exams]

accepted.s: During the 2013 taper tantrum, Morgan Stanley included India among the:
accepted.x: Morgan Stanley described India as one of the ‘Fragile Five’ during the 2013 taper tantrum because of external-sector vulnerability.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive group label associated with the external shock.
accepted.sec: Capital flight and external vulnerability  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched with weak net capital flows?
o: Lower outward FDI, higher portfolio inflows and reduced private-equity exits; outward FDI rose 75 per cent to $127 billion
IPO exits by PE/VC, rising FPI purchases and lower US tariffs; outward FDI fell to $7.6 billion
Higher remittances, stronger FPI inflows and US tariff cuts; outward FDI rose to $44.0 billion
IPO exits by PE/VC, FPI sell-offs and US tariffs; outward FDI rose 75 per cent to $29.2 billion
accepted.x: Weak net capital was associated with PE/VC IPO exits, FPI sell-offs and US tariffs. Outward FDI rose by 75 per cent to $29.2 billion.
accepted.tq: Use the correctly matched cluster of causes and the associated outward-FDI figure.
accepted.sec: Capital flight and external vulnerability  [other exams]

accepted.s: In January 2026, India’s foreign-exchange reserves of $701.4 billion covered approximately what proportion of external debt?
accepted.x: Foreign-exchange reserves of $701.4 billion in January 2026 covered about 94 per cent of India’s external debt.
accepted.tq: Associate the reserve figure with its stated coverage ratio rather than treating reserves as exceeding debt.
accepted.sec: Capital flight and external vulnerability  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes current account convertibility from capital account convertibility?
o: Capital account convertibility covers remittances only, while current account convertibility covers government borrowing
Current account convertibility covers trade, income and transfers, while capital account convertibility covers FDI, portfolio investment and borrowing
Current account convertibility concerns FDI, while capital account convertibility concerns only merchandise trade
Both forms of convertibility concern only official foreign-exchange reserves
accepted.x: Current account convertibility permits free conversion for trade, income and transfers. Capital account convertibility relates to FDI, portfolio investment and borrowing.
accepted.tq: Separate routine international transactions from transactions involving assets and liabilities.
accepted.sec: Convertibility - current vs capital, year, committees  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to exchange-rate reform in India in chronological order:
A. Unified exchange rate introduced
B. LERMS introduced
C. Full current account convertibility accepted through Article VIII of the IMF
D. Second Tarapore Committee set up
accepted.x: LERMS was introduced in 1992-93, the unified rate was introduced on 1 March 1993, full current account convertibility followed in August 1994, and the second Tarapore Committee was set up in 2006.
accepted.tq: Fix the sequence using the dated milestones before placing the later committee.
accepted.sec: Convertibility - current vs capital, year, committees  [other exams]

accepted.s: Under the Liberalised Exchange Rate Management System (LERMS), the exchange rate was determined through which arrangement?
o: 60 per cent official rate and 40 per cent market rate
40 per cent official rate and 60 per cent market rate
100 per cent market rate from the beginning
accepted.x: LERMS, introduced in the 1992-93 Budget, used a dual exchange-rate system comprising 40 per cent official rate and 60 per cent market rate.
accepted.tq: Remember the direction of the two percentages instead of reversing the official and market shares.
accepted.sec: Convertibility - current vs capital, year, committees  [other exams]

accepted.s: India achieved full current account convertibility in August 1994 by:
o: Setting up the second Tarapore Committee
Accepting Article VIII of the IMF
accepted.x: Full current account convertibility was achieved in August 1994 when India accepted the obligations under Article VIII of the IMF.
accepted.tq: Match the convertibility milestone with the specific IMF provision rather than with a domestic statute.
accepted.sec: Convertibility - current vs capital, year, committees  [other exams]

accepted.s: The second committee on capital account convertibility was set up by the Reserve Bank of India on:
accepted.x: The RBI set up the second Tarapore Committee on 31 July 2006.
accepted.tq: Use the exact committee-constitution date and distinguish it from the dates of FEMA and exchange-rate reforms.
accepted.sec: Convertibility - current vs capital, year, committees  [other exams]

accepted.s: India delinked the rupee from sterling in:
accepted.x: The Indian rupee was delinked from sterling in September 1975.
accepted.tq: Recall the historical exchange-rate milestone independently of the later convertibility reforms.
accepted.sec: Convertibility - current vs capital, year, committees  [other exams]
